evidence.quote: They published the critics' list of "[[List of films considered the best|greatest films]]" based on 846 critics, programmers, academics, and distributors,<ref name="bfi">{{cite web |title=The 100 Greatest Films of All Time |url=https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/greatest-films-all-time |website=Sight & Sound |publisher=BFI |access-date=23 March 2020}}</ref> as well as a directors' list based on 358 directors and filmmakers.<ref name="director2012">{{cite web |url=https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/polls/greatest-films-all-time/directors-100-best |title=Directors' 10 Greatest Films of All Time |work=Sight & Sound |publisher=British Film Institute |date=December 4, 2014}}</ref> The two lists were headed by 1958's ''[[Vertigo (film)|Vertigo]]'' and 1953's ''[[Tokyo Story]]'' respectively.
evidence.semantics: The two lists were headed by Vertigo and Tokyo Story respectively: directors' list is the second list, so Tokyo Story is its explicitly asserted leader.

assumptions: Scope is every film selection explicitly asserted in the captured Critics' poll section, including the directors' leader in its introductory prose. Tokyo Story therefore has two distinct memberships. A critics-only consumer should filter category rather than erase this second assertion.

Position is within category, preserving critics' source list order (1–10) and following runner-up (11). Directors' position 1 follows its prose assertion of leadership. Position is not a separately printed source rank.
Top-ten ranks follow the uninterrupted ordered-list numbering. No ties are stated and vote counts differ; tie false represents no tie asserted in this captured selection.
Battleship Potemkin is retained as explicitly named closest runner-up. Its numeric rank is left null because not printed; rank 11 would be a derived inference from its relationship to the top ten.

Vertigo's prose/caption mentions and Man with a Movie Camera's prose mention duplicate their critics' memberships, so no duplicate records are added. Citizen Kane's previous-five-polls first-place history is contextual, not five separately identifiable current list selections. Reference titles and image names do not add selections.

The section reports 2,045 films received mentions but names only the ten ranked critics' selections plus their closest runner-up and the directors' leader. This is an incomplete published subset of the broader polls, not evidence that unnamed entries were extracted or that all 2,045 memberships are recoverable.

This extraction covers the named explicit selections in the supplied section only. It does not assert original BFI accuracy, source independence, complete underlying poll coverage, or human audit quality.
